newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran oil marketing centres on Europe and Asia.
newsitem.headline: Iran oil marketing centres on Europe and Asia.

text.p: Iran is marketing 80 percent of its crude equally between European and Asian markets, Hojjatollah Ghanimifard, head of international affairs at the National Iranian Oil Company (NIOC) said on Monday.

"We almost have a sort of balance of the market for the Iranian crude which means that we have almost 40 percent of the crude going to the Asian market, 40 percent going to Europe and 20 percent to the African and American continents," he told Reuters in an interview.

NIOC exports an average of 2.5 million barrels per day (bpd) of crude oil to markets east and west of Suez, mainly to refiners through liftings from the Kharg Island export terminal in the Gulf and by delivered sales by its affiliates.

Ghanimifard said that NIOC had overcome U.S. sanctions imposed in June 1995 -- which prohibited American firms from lifting Iranian crude -- by securing increased sales to non-U.S. refiners in Europe as well as China and India in Asia.
"We have proved that the marketing strategy of NIOC, when we changed it (following U.S. sanctions), was a proper one and we could replace American refiners and traders," he said.

U.S. firms were lifting nearly a quarter of Iran's crude exports before Washington imposed a comprehensive trade and investment ban against Iran for its alleged support of international terrorism and desire for nuclear weapons.
Iran has repeatedly denied the U.S. charges.
